Problem: A termite eats its way along the diagonal from point P to point Q in a 3 x 4 x 5 cuboid consisting of 60 identical small cubes. The diagonal does not intersect the edges of any small cube inside the cuboid. How many small cubes does the termite pass through on its journey? Express your answer as a whole number.

<reflection>
The cuboid is 3 x 4 x 5 and consists of 60 identical unit cubes. The termite travels along a space diagonal from P to Q. The diagonal does not intersect any small cube edges inside the cuboid. The dimensions correspond to 3 layers, 4 layers, and 5 layers in the three directions.
This misdefines the subtraction in the 3D cube-counting formula. The correct adjustment is based on simultaneous crossings of internal coordinate planes, not simply on intersections with small-cube edges; in this problem the diagonal has no interior edge intersections, yet the correct count still requires subtracting 2, not treating gaps as edge overlaps.
Count the distinct interior grid-plane crossings along the diagonal, or apply the correct gcd-based 3D cube-counting formula.
</reflection>
